candidates.why: Pre-registered winner's-curse quantification validated on nine oracle settings with Holm-corrected p-values, 200 gold-set splits, and honestly reported negative results on acceptance rules.
candidates.caveat: Scope is instruction rewriting on three tasks with deterministic scoring; the 64-item audit removes average bias but leaves per-setting errors of -8.5 to +5.8 points and RMSE of reported gains still 5.7 points.

candidates.why: Headline '214 solved' is LLM-self-certified (only 4 of 420 STOC outputs author-verified) and the paper concedes no control arm of direct model use, so the central claim is untested.
candidates.caveat: The key ablation is missing: no comparison with direct use of the underlying models on the same 3,800 problems, and cross-collection comparisons are confounded by model, rounds, and corpus.

candidates.why: Headline bundles the admission gate with an AFE search expansion whose ablated-only variant falls below PiEvo (60.60 vs 64.78), so the gate's isolated contribution is never cleanly shown; SQ normalization is arbitrary.
candidates.caveat: Triage-only falls to 60.60 SQ, below PiEvo's 64.78, and SQ is normalized by per-task references the authors admit are not attainable upper bounds, with several backbone margins within ~1 sigma at 24 evaluations and 3 seeds.

candidates.why: The beta2-schedule win is a 0.07% relative loss improvement on one model/dataset/seed with constants manually fitted from the very run being explained; the simulation predicts propensity, not spike timing.
candidates.caveat: The paper's own figures show the first-order Taylor term decreasing ~20x faster than any layer-wise quadratic model predicts, and the authors call the equivalent-batch-factor cancellation 'somehow magical'.

candidates.why: Pre-registered protocol, leave-one-seed-out calibration, a below-gate negative control, and honest negative results (no lead in 8/9 folds, false alarms conceded) supporting a consequential metric-audit finding, cleanly replicated for its one mechanism.
candidates.caveat: Every number is Qwen3-0.6B and the inversion rests on a single replicated mechanism (duplicate_data, 3 seeds); two calibration seeds cannot certify the union bound and the held-out branch false-alarms in all three folds.

candidates.why: Four-page industrial report gives only relative-% deltas with no confidence intervals, a baseline known to diverge, a 28,000-fold figure framed against diverged trainsets, and effectively zero reproducibility.
candidates.caveat: No absolute AUC/RMSE, no significance tests despite 12 A/A arms, no comparison against established stability baselines, and the model, data, and configurations are proprietary.

candidates.why: Propagation of reward hacking is demonstrated with source controls (RL-only and SDF-only near zero), chain vs no-justification contrasts (R=3.40 vs 0.14), and a feedback-channel experiment that unlocks propagation in refusing models.
candidates.caveat: The amplification headline (R=3.40) comes from a curated hard-task, justification-bearing regime while the full-task-set estimate is R=0.60, and the confirmed-hack detector covers only three hand-catalogued mechanisms.

candidates.why: Solid avg@32 math gains over re-implemented baselines, but at 3-4B scale, single-seed-looking runs with no variance, and search wins that lean on two benchmarks while losing PopQA and 2Wiki.
candidates.caveat: All baselines are re-implementations inside the authors' strengthened PPO recipe, the coordination hypothesis is confirmed only softly on a coarse grid, and Proposition 1's corrected target is knowingly biased.

candidates.why: A deliberate strawman (reward is 100% surface features with zero correctness weight) that self-describes as replicating Gao et al. 2022 in a new domain, on a single seed and single 8B model.
candidates.caveat: The conditional-accuracy 'most consequential finding' rests on ~35 committed answers with a Wilson CI spanning 19 points, and the theorem characterises the authors' own construction as much as a general phenomenon.

candidates.why: Hundreds of thousands of controlled comparisons isolate padding as the dominant flip factor, and pretrained rotary/NoPE controls confirm the learned-absolute-position cause; mitigations are measured with a validated margin certificate on 4,644 held-out flips.
candidates.caveat: Headline magnitudes come from small from-scratch GPT-2-style models (pretrained Qwen3/ModernBERT flip zero labels from padding), and mitigation costs are measured in the experimental setup, not production.

candidates.why: Developer-confirmed bugs with matched budgets and 10 runs per config, but only 7 of 55 reports were fixed and the paper's own ablation shows the non-data-flow operator pool beats the TFG pool, undercutting the novelty story.
candidates.caveat: The CG-derived pool alone beats the TFG-derived pool on every metric including the paper's own data-flow diversity measure, and external validity is limited to two frameworks on CPU/one-GPU.

candidates.why: Budget-matched controls are careful, but the finding that worst-case search beats random sampling is near-tautological by the authors' own admission and everything rests on an uncalibrated, idealized simulation with no hardware.
candidates.caveat: On the more realistic REAL configuration the searched/MC ratio drops to 0.67-2.70 with four models falling below 1, code is only available on request, and PGD endpoints are flagged by the authors as likely start-point artifacts.

candidates.why: 15,882 injected faults with full propagation accounting, a matched-unit comparison showing topology changes recover 19-27% of failures vs 0.2-4.5% for model swaps, and complementary protection mechanisms with quantified coverage.
candidates.caveat: All results come from three AutoGen workflow topologies with a within-family model set (no frontier-tier model), and the 20.7% silent-failure headline depends on the authors' own script-defined adjudication.

candidates.why: CI-bounded prevalence estimate plus a controlled experiment with an unrelated-skill control isolating similarity as the cause, a 96% effective hook intervention, 88.9% re-run agreement, and a partial Codex replication.
candidates.caveat: Fidelity is fidelity-to-an-LLM's-reading of skill prose, each (model, configuration, pair) cell is a single run, and the headline 1-in-4 prevalence rests on public repositories only.

candidates.why: Well-validated LLM-judge localization (kappa 0.70-0.74 vs humans) but the central construct has no gold standard, 87 of 95 cases come from 15 CVEfixes tasks, and judges share families with evaluated agents.
candidates.caveat: The missed-opportunity headline (59/95) rests on the two least-stable dimensions (cross-judge alpha 0.68), and repeatability (alpha 0.96) should not be read as correctness.

candidates.why: Concrete catches (two empty kernels passing tolerance tests, honestly decomposed 64.3% mutation-detection rate), but the proof guarantee leans on unverified hand review of specification tightness and the full-pipeline sample is 14 of 100 with under-specified selection.
candidates.caveat: A spec that is not tight reduces the guarantee to 'both programs are safe', there is no automated tightness certification, and 26 of 51 mutation misses are intra-warp conflicts beyond NVBit's reach.

candidates.why: Forensic-quality audit with byte-for-byte code accounting across three released ternary models, a documented 58.79-to-0.78% export collapse explained at the code level, a 32x learning-rate control showing the effect is regime-specific, and pre-declared non-inferiority remedies.
candidates.caveat: The headline collapse holds in a narrow low-LR corner (at 32x the rate there is no detectable change), and the 512 GSM8K prompts are carved from the official training split.

candidates.why: Careful LTT-based certification with validity comparisons against five selectors, but the guarantee rests on i.i.d. scenes from 500 fixed simulator resets per suite, and tight budgets force 56-100% fallback to the reference policy.
candidates.caveat: Simulation-only pairing is undemonstrated on real robots where exact resets are impossible, and the Crafter evidence covers only two tasks with three seeds, one of which fails certification on a seed.

candidates.why: Clean natural-range manipulation and passing positive controls, but rescue was not run for either audited Gemma latent, so the headline 'latents barely change behavior' rests on removal fractions that are only lower bounds.
candidates.caveat: Scope is three small models and three clean single-concept tasks, all headline deltas flow through a single LLM judge, and the full codebase is only 'released upon publication'.

candidates.why: Quantifies the activation-vs-intervention gap for SAE discovery scores (median |alpha/beta| 2.8-4.6%) with BH-corrected tests, a noise-only simulation, and a prespecified contrast showing attribution predicts realized interventions far better than probe coefficients.
candidates.caveat: The headline 91-97% vs 17-35% sign comparison is partly mechanical for latents that never fire at the probed position, scope is one SAE at one layer per model on eleven toy tasks, and the Stein-residual intervals cover only 0.82 at nominal 95%.

candidates.why: Striking probe re-audits (Othello floor above the classic probe), but the meta-analysis testbed tops out at 794k parameters, LLM-audit floors are reconstructed from n-gram descriptions of inputs, and no code artifact is linked.
candidates.caveat: The NYC conclusion that published scores fall below the 0.33 floor depends on the n-gram feature choice, ceilings are set to 1 for the published-probe audits, and the U_H=-0.30 Othello case exposes an unhandled regime.

candidates.why: Large simulation campaign with matching theory, but no hardware evaluation despite the Tofino implementation, and the 16-39x headline is CCT inflation over an idealized lower bound in the authors' own simulator.
candidates.caveat: The 3-4x DCTCP explosion for REPS/AR is partly a simulator artifact the authors themselves drop, and the striking Theta(m) result requires synchronized permutation collectives far from real workloads.

candidates.why: Rare production fleet reliability data with clean isolation tests, but the 12x improvement is measured during a 130x fleet ramp and ends at parity (not superiority) with an anonymized, unverifiable vendor baseline.
candidates.caveat: The in-house diagnostic accuracy is 49.2% (wrong more often than right), the TCP-retransmit comparison is partially apples-to-oranges across flow-control strategies, and vendor baselines cannot be externally re-verified.

candidates.why: Production latency/CPU numbers are real, but the only baseline is untuned kernel TCP, the headline training win depends entirely on one software knob (hardware-only RDMA is worse than TCP), and both workloads are proprietary ByteDance jobs.
candidates.caveat: The authors admit a differently configured TCP baseline could recover much of the gap, inference gains are PS-level proxies rather than end-to-end service latency, and there is no production ablation for QP multiplexing or receive credits.

candidates.why: Candid system card with a genuinely clean router-drift control experiment and disclosed $2.6M RL spend, but the largest headline deltas are against the team's own previous generation and 3 of ~14 benchmarks are in-house with self-hosted graders.
candidates.caveat: Where third-party numbers exist the frontier still leads (ExploitGym 17.8 vs 30.3, ExploitBench 47.9 vs 70.0, Terminal Bench 4.0 34.9 vs 49.0), CyberGym numbers use a self-redesigned oracle, and flagship weights are not released.

candidates.why: Unusually honest open-weights report, but the 'leads fully open models' framing rests on a peer set that excludes Qwen3.5-9B, which beats it on nearly every knowledge and math benchmark, and a key ablation is cited rather than run.
candidates.caveat: HarmBench attack success worsened from 8.7%/2.8% to 26.5% with human jailbreaks at 31.5%, and the 70B was stopped at half its multimodal mixture for production reasons.
